---
author: 
id: B_238
internalId: 0f3edcd4-a27e-45e8-a6f1-4f3cf25cb096
title: backend detects card state change
status: ready for implementation
owner: 
affects:

policy:
---
Detect the card state transition that ends an action on the backend instead of routing it through a renderer. Split from [B\_235](B_235_end_of_action_not_logged.md).

## Current state

An agent finishes work by writing a new `status` into the card markdown header. Auto-finish and schedule triggers must react to that write.

Today the detection round-trips through the UI. The backend watcher `watchProject` (`desktop/src/project/project_files.js:400`) sees the file change and forwards it to the renderer through `local_bridge_dispatch.js:314`. The renderer reloads the card, parses the header, compares `previousCard.header.status` against the new value (`app/src/services/data/data_service.ts:561`, and the card-operations callback at `:162-170`), and calls back into the backend through `notifyActionCardStateChange`. That lands at `local_bridge_dispatch.js:454` and fans out to `ActionRunnerService.handleCardStateChange` (`action_runner_service.js:351`) and `ActionSchedulerService.handleCardStateChange` (`action_scheduler_service.js:194`).

Every connected window runs that comparison, so with two windows open the same transition is reported twice and `requestAutoFinish` (`action_run.js:273`) can fire twice for one run. With no window focused on the card, or a window mid-reload, it can arrive late or not at all. Nothing under `desktop/src` reads a card markdown header today; the backend resolves cards by `cardInternalId` everywhere but never loads one from disk.

## implementation details

* Add backend card-header reading: for a changed card file, parse the frontmatter and extract `internalId` and `status`. Reuse the shared parsing used by the renderer rather than writing a second parser.
* Backend keeps the last known status per `internalId` and calls `handleCardStateChange` itself only on an actual transition. Both consumers, run auto-finish and the scheduler, move together.
* Remove `notifyActionCardStateChange` from the renderer, from the bridge dispatch, and from the preload surface. The renderer no longer participates in auto-finish.
* Handle card rename and move without emitting a spurious transition: identity is `internalId`, not path. A deleted card drops its remembered status.
* Handle the card file being written by the backend itself the same way as an external write; the trigger is the resulting status, not the writer.
* Tests: two connected renderers produce exactly one auto-finish; a transition with no renderer attached still triggers; rename with unchanged status triggers nothing; repeated identical writes trigger once; scheduler and auto-finish both observe the same single transition.

## acceptance criteria

* Card state transitions are detected on the backend from the card file, with no renderer involvement.
* One transition produces exactly one auto-finish request regardless of how many windows are open, including none.
* Renaming or moving a card produces no state transition.
* Scheduler triggers and action auto-finish consume the same backend-detected transition.

entries.content:
Read spec + code. Plan below. No edits yet.

## Findings

Today the chain is: `watchProject` (`desktop/src/project/project_files.js:400`) → renderer → `DataService.dispatchCardChanges` (`app/src/services/data/data_service.ts:561`) compares `previousCard.header.status` → `notifyActionCardStateChange` → `local_bridge_dispatch.js:454` → scheduler + runner. Every window runs that comparison, so N windows produce N auto-finish requests, and zero windows produce none.

Nothing in `desktop/src` parses a card header today. The one existing backend frontmatter reader (`desktop/src/actions/activity/card_activity_reference.js`) is a write-oriented line splicer, not a field parser. The real parser is `parseHeaderFields`/`splitHeader` in `app/src/services/data/markdown_parsing_service.ts`, renderer-only TypeScript. `shared/*.mjs` is the established both-sides home (desktop `require()`s those `.mjs` files directly), so that is where the parser goes.

## Change plan — 5 blocks

**Block 1 — shared header parser**
Move `splitHeader`, `parseHeaderFields` and their list/map helpers out of `markdown_parsing_service.ts` into `shared/markdown_header_fields.mjs` (+ `.d.mts`). `markdown_parsing_service.ts` imports them, behavior unchanged. Tests: existing `markdown_parsing_service.node.test.ts` must stay green; add `shared` unit tests for frontmatter split, CRLF, missing/broken header.

**Block 2 — backend card state tracker**
New `desktop/src/actions/card/card_state_tracker.js`. It holds `statusByInternalId` plus `pathsByInternalId`, and exposes `seed(files)`, `observeChange({ changeKind, path })`, `reset()`. Rules: identity is `internalId`, never path; a first-ever observation of an `internalId` records the status and fires nothing; a later different status fires one transition; an identical rewrite fires nothing; a `removed` path drops that path, and drops the remembered status only when no path for that `internalId` remains. That last rule makes rename/move silent in either event order. Tests: `card_state_tracker.test.mjs` covering repeated identical writes, rename, move, delete, unparseable file, non-card markdown.

**Block 3 — wiring in the backend**
In `local_bridge_dispatch.js`: seed the tracker during `activateProject` (line ~106, using `projectPaths.projectFolder`) so a status written after startup has a known predecessor; feed the `watchProject` `onChange` callback (line ~313) into the tracker; on a transition call `actionSchedulerService.handleCardStateChange` then `actionRunnerService.handleCardStateChange` — the same single transition, same order as today. Delete the `notifyActionCardStateChange` dispatch entry (`:454`) and its `preload.js:101` name. Tests: update `local_bridge_dispatch.test.mjs` — one file write reaches scheduler and runner exactly once with no renderer call; rename triggers nothing; two attached renderers are irrelevant because they no longer participate.

**Block 4 — renderer removal**
Remove `notifyActionCardStateChange` from `action_run_registry.ts:362`, the two call sites in `data_service.ts` (`:167`, `:562`), `electron_action_bridge.ts:174`, and `remote_control_storage_service.ts:711`. `triggerStateActions` at `data_service.ts:161` is a different feature and stays. Tests: drop the removed cases from `action_run_registry.node.test.ts`, `remote_control_storage_service.node.test.ts`, `preload.test.mjs`; keep the rest green.

**Block 5 — close out**
Run `npm run typecheck` plus both vitest suites, then set `status: ready` in `B_238_backend_detects_card_state_change.md`.

## One decision for you

Seeding (Block 3) reads every card markdown file in the project folder once at project activation, backend-side. Without it, the first status write after startup has no remembered predecessor and would not fire auto-finish. That is the same read the renderer already does at load, so the cost is a duplicate scan, not a new class of work. Approve that, or prefer a lazier seed?

Approve and I implement blocks 1→5 in order.
